extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to support open scientific research in computational linguistics. It includes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The corpus was built by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, then processing the PDFs into structured full text and enriching the data using Semantic Scholar's API. The dataset undergoes annual updates by monitoring URL changes for new additions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some fields are only available for a portion of papers; for example, only 16.8% of papers have an arXiv paper ID. The paper also notes that full-text extraction fails mostly for papers between 2000 and 2015.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, plus additional information fetched from Semantic Scholar's Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 1952 to September 2022 for the corpus contents; annual updates are performed thereafter.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PDF files were processed into structured full text using GROBID; figures and tables were extracted from PDFs using PDFFigures; citation network information was constructed using internal citations and external citation counts from Semantic Scholar; language was detected using a public language detection toolkit; topic labels were predicted using trained models and released as silver labels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Full-text extraction was performed from PDFs, and the resulting data were organized into a Semantic Scholar-style schema and additionally provided in CSV and Apache Parquet formats.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper does not describe manual annotation for the ACL OCL corpus itself. For the separate Scientific Topic Dataset (STop), topic labels were crawled from conference websites and aligned with ACL OCL papers; these labels were used as ground truth for topic classification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Model-predicted topic labels are described as silver labels and are released together with OCL. The paper reports that 13 of 15 top-cited papers had correct predicted labels in a case study.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, Semantic Scholar Graph API, langdetect, BART-large-MNLI, TF-IDF, YAKE!, SciBERT, SPECTER
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, and the authors state that they plan to update OCL by year to keep it current with ACL Anthology data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus is intended to advance open science and reproducibility in computational linguistics, support bibliographic and trend analysis, and enable downstream research such as information extraction, summarization, topic analysis, and multimodal research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is biased toward peer-reviewed and open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology, and the topic analysis notes a bias in top-cited papers toward dominant topics such as machine translation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus is small-scale and limited to ACL Anthology sources, so it is not comprehensive like S2ORC. It does not include other sources beyond ACL Anthology. Full-text extraction has quality issues such as missing section names, merged paragraphs, footnote mixing, and missed figures/tables. The corpus is unlabeled for specific tasks requiring labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for training, testing, validation, and downstream research in computational linguistics, including metadata analysis, bibliographic research, topic classification, temporal topic trend analysis, document-level information extraction, related work generation, summarization, citation analysis, multimodal research, and knowledge graph construction.
